experiment: Exp 13B cross-architecture validation: dense no-QK-Norm models plus MoE/Mamba/looped structural audits
gpu_assignment: container-visible xpu:0 backed exclusively by host GPU1 (<card-node> <render-node>); no GPU0 device nodes mounted

method.evaluation: full-depth exact fixed-window evaluation, 2x2044 scored tokens (WikiText-2 and Python code), streaming vocab logits in chunks
method.calibration: strict mixed WT2+Python calibration rows, pos0-excluded analytical BiasCorr unless labeled pos0incl; 0/0 6-gram overlap with both eval domains
method.statistics: paired 32-token block bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, 95% CIs; negative control is exact sign-flipped -b
method.tokenizer_note: the same source text windows were tokenized independently per tokenizer, so exact token-ID SHA-256 values differ across architectures by necessity
method.reference_validation: manual layer-by-layer BF16 streaming was checked against direct model.forward for both dense models: WT2 NLL matched exactly to printed precision and final logit maxdiff was 0.0 (Qwen2.5 NLL 2.5070071220/PPL 12.26816; SmolLM2 NLL 2.3728237152/PPL 10.72764)
method.proxy_scope: dense-model embeddings, norms and lm_head remain BF16/unquantized as in Exp7B proxy methodology; decoder linear weights are quantized

supported: HadHF-G16 beats SymINT4-G128 RTN data-free in both dense architectures and domains, significant

W4A8 is statistically tied with W4A16 in three of four dense domain comparisons; the exception is a small but significant SmolLM2 code regression (+0.00388 KL), so no material consistent activation-quality penalty was detected
not_universal: HadHF-G16 beats MLX-asym-G64 significantly in Qwen2.5 but is a tie/non-significant difference in SmolLM2
HadHF-G16 beats NVFP4-4/6 in Qwen2.5 but loses to NVFP4-4/6 in SmolLM2; therefore no universal format ordering across dense architectures

supported: Sign-flipped -b controls are worse than data-free baselines in essentially every comparison, often catastrophically in SmolLM2, validating that the mean-error direction is real

direct pos0-included versus pos0-excluded pairs usually differ by only about 0.0004-0.003 KL, but they are not universally null: a few small significant effects appear in both directions and there is no consistent winner
not_universal: Qwen2.5: pos0-excluded BiasCorr helps SymINT4, MLX-asym and NVFP4 significantly, but significantly hurts HadHF-G16

SmolLM2: positive BiasCorr significantly hurts every tested format even though -b is far worse; this indicates correct sign but harmful magnitude/interaction in a small no-QK-Norm Llama model, not a universal win
Therefore Finding B is architecture- and quantizer-dependent; it cannot be claimed as universally beneficial

finding_C_meanx_and_attention.mean_x_law: input-projection families (q/k/v and gate/up) have higher WT2-vs-code mean_x cosine than output/down projections in both dense architectures; the effect is especially extreme in SmolLM2 q/k/v (mean cosine 0.937) versus Qwen2.5 (0.686)
finding_C_meanx_and_attention.k_v_asymmetry: the attention asymmetry reverses across architectures: in Qwen2.5 K-only quantization is significantly worse than V-only (WT2 delta +0.01318 KL), while in SmolLM2 K-only is significantly better than V-only (WT2 delta -0.02769 KL); in Qwen3.8 K-only minus V-only WT2 delta is -0.00171 KL (significant=True). There is no universal K-more-sensitive-than-V law.

evidence.conclusion: INVALID BF16 REFERENCE: every checked routed-expert tensor in layers 0, 1, 20, and 39 is exactly zero, while shared/non-expert tensors match the GPTQ checkpoint bit-exactly. Therefore heretic-BF16-dequant cannot be used as a MoE reference and no valid BF16 vs GPTQ MoE quality comparison is possible from local checkpoints.

gptq_quantization_layout.unquantized_or_dense_tensors: linear_attn.in_proj_a/b remain dense BF16 weights; MoE router model.language_model.layers.N.mlp.gate.weight remains dense; embeddings/lm_head/norms/conv tensors remain dense
gptq_quantization_layout.dimension_compatibility: hidden_size=2048, expert moe_intermediate_size=512, shared_expert_intermediate_size=512, and linear-attention projected input dimensions are all divisible by 128; no Nemotron-style K%128 edge case in the core Qwen3.6 MoE dimensions
gptq_quantization_layout.gptq_config: bits=4, sym=true, group_size=128, desc_act=false, static_groups=false, true_sequential=true, act_group_aware=true, gptqmodel 7.1.0-dev

qwen36_moe.disk_constraint: a true BF16 Qwen3.6-35B-A3B reference would require roughly 70 GB and cannot be downloaded within the available /data budget; quantized checkpoints cannot serve as their own reference without circularity

nemotron_h.gptq_zero_point_convention_observed: unpacked qzeros are 0 in sampled Nemotron tensors; qweight integer mean is approximately 8, so effective symmetric zero-point 8 was used for structural dequantization (unlike the Qwen3.8 GPTQModel checkpoint whose stored zeros are 7 under the zeros+1 convention)
nemotron_h.critical_edge_case: all routed-expert down_proj inputs have K=1856, so K % 128 = 64; Had128-style exact 128-input rotation blocks cannot tile those matrices without padding or a padded/mixed-block design, while GPTQ G64 fits exactly
